questions.q: This lesson describes two ways to run dbt in CI. What are they?
options: A hand-rolled GitHub Actions workflow (from the Git/CI/CD course) or dbt Cloud's built-in CI job
Only GitHub Actions can run dbt in CI
Only dbt Cloud can run dbt automatically, GitHub Actions cannot
There is exactly one way, and it requires no configuration at all
questions.explain: Lesson 21 of the Git/GitHub/CI-CD course covers hand-rolling it with GitHub Actions; dbt Cloud's own CI job configuration gets you the same result without writing that YAML.

questions.q: What does a dbt Cloud CI run build into, and why does that matter?
options: A temporary schema scoped to that specific pull request, so the run never touches dev or prod
The production schema directly, the same as a scheduled run
No schema at all — it only lints the SQL
A schema shared by every open pull request at once
questions.explain: dbt Cloud creates a temp schema per PR, builds into it, then discards it — a failing or passing CI check never affects the tables dashboards actually query.

questions.q: Why does this lesson (and Lesson 21 of the Git/CI/CD course) recommend `dbt build` over separate `dbt run` and `dbt test` commands in CI?
options: dbt build runs seeds, models, tests, and snapshots together in dependency order, stopping downstream work when an upstream test fails
dbt build is simply a faster alias with no behavioral difference
dbt run and dbt test cannot be used in a CI environment at all
dbt build skips tests entirely to save time
questions.explain: Because dbt build respects dependency order and stops downstream builds on an upstream test failure, a CI red X is more likely to mean something is actually broken.

questions.q: What is the goal shared by both the GitHub Actions approach and dbt Cloud's built-in CI job?
options: Run dbt build against the changed code before the pull request merges, so problems surface as a PR check, not a broken production table
Skip testing until after the merge to save CI minutes
Automatically merge every pull request regardless of test results
Replace the need for pull requests entirely
questions.explain: Both paths exist to catch a broken model or failing test before it merges, rather than discovering it in production the next morning.

questions.q: What does dbt Cloud's built-in CI job save you from doing, compared to the GitHub Actions approach from the Git/CI/CD course?
options: Writing your own ci.yml, generating a profiles.yml from env vars, and wiring up GitHub Secrets for the connection
Nothing — the two approaches require identical manual setup
Writing any dbt models at all
Committing your code to Git in the first place
questions.explain: dbt Cloud already has the warehouse connection configured, so its CI job needs none of the ci.yml/profiles.yml/Secrets plumbing that a hand-rolled GitHub Actions workflow requires.
